name: Fandral Staghelm
summary: From the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle. With Malfurion Stormrage gone into the Emerald Dream, Fandral championed Teldrassil and a forceful Kaldorei resurgence, often clashing with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind.

sections.title: Architect of Teldrassil
sections.body:
After the Third War, the night elves lost their immortality and sacred sanctuary when Nordrassil was sacrificed atop Mount Hyjal. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids. He persuaded the Circle of Ancients that their people must rebuild and regain their immortality.

With the Circle's approval, Fandral led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He meant its great bough to honor Kaldorei endurance and restore their lost supremacy. The Dragon Aspects withheld their blessings from the endeavor.

sections.title: Tragedy in the Shifting Sands
sections.body:
A millennium before the First War, Fandral served as the Kaldorei field commander in Silithus during the War of the Shifting Sands. The qiraji knew him as Kar'sis, the Hand of Earth. His beloved only son, Valstann, fought beside him on the front lines.

The qiraji General Rajaxx exploited Fandral's devotion with a feint against Southwind Village. Valstann was captured and executed before the horrified Archdruid. Grief broke Fandral's spirit and drove a devastating retreat. His bitter hatred of the swarm endures.

sections.title: Rivalry and Hubris
sections.body: In Darnassus, Fandral governs Kaldorei affairs with a haughty, unyielding hand. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind is a spiritual leader who favors preservation and cautious diplomacy. Fandral instead sees military expansion and decisive strength as vital to his people's survival.

faq.answer: Fandral is the acting Archdruid of the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus, leading Kaldorei druids while Malfurion Stormrage is absent. His fiery temper and imperial ambitions drive his vision for Teldrassil.

faq.q: Why doesn't Fandral get along with Tyrande?
aliases: why do druids and priestesses disagree
faq.answer: Fandral favors Kaldorei military resurgence, aggressive expansion, and the return of their lost immortality. Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people through spiritual devotion to Elune and caution. Their opposing visions for the night elves after Hyjal fuel fierce political friction in Darnassus.

After the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil was scarred and the night elves lost their immortality. With Malfurion missing, Fandral persuaded the Circle of Ancients that their people must rebuild and regain it. With the Circle's approval, Fandral and the most powerful druids grew Teldrassil.

During the War of the Shifting Sands in Silithus, Fandral's son Valstann was lured into an ambush at Southwind Village. The qiraji general Rajaxx captured and killed him before Fandral. The loss left the Archdruid grief-stricken and bitter.

faq.q: Where can Fandral Staghelm be found?
faq.answer: Fandral can be found atop the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, surrounded by his loyal druids as he oversees the Kaldorei capital.

angles.text: As a Druid, you see Staghelm command the Darnassian druids and press the Cenarion Circle toward direct worldly authority. He clashes with the traditional teachings of the sleeping Malfurion Stormrage.
As a Night Elf, you see Fandral embody Kaldorei pride and fury. He drives the settlement of Teldrassil, while ordinary citizens feel the rift between his enclave and the Temple of the Moon.

As an Alliance member, you find Teldrassil a bastion in northern Kalimdor. Staghelm views the younger races with thinly veiled disdain and tolerates their presence only when political expediency demands it.
